entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7283"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 6</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Prov.6.1-Prov.6.35">Pr 6:1-35</reference>. After admonitions against suretyship and sloth (compare <reference osisRef="Prov.6.6-Prov.6.8">Pr 6:6-8</reference>), the character and fate of the wicked generally are set forth, and the writer (<reference osisRef="Prov.6.20-Prov.6.35">Pr 6:20-35</reference>) resumes the warnings against incontinence, pointing out its certain and terrible results. This train of thought seems to intimate the kindred of these vices.</title> <div sID="gen11240" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7283"/><hi type="bold">1-2. if--</hi>The condition extends through both verses.<div eID="gen11240" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen11241" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">be surety--</hi>art pledged.<div eID="gen11241" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen11242" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">stricken ... hand--</hi>bargained (compare <reference osisRef="Job.17.3">Job 17:3</reference>).<div eID="gen11242" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen11243" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">with a stranger--</hi>that is, for a friend (compare <reference osisRef="Prov.11.15">Pr 11:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.17.18">17:18</reference>). <div eID="gen11243" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 6 Pr 6:1-35 . After admonitions against suretyship and sloth (compare Pr 6:6-8 ), the character and fate of the wicked generally are set forth, and the writer ( Pr 6:20-35 ) resumes the warnings against incontinence, pointing out its certain and terrible results. This train of thought seems to intimate the kindred of these vices. 1-2. if-- The condition extends through both verses. be surety-- art pledged. stricken ... hand-- bargained (compare Job 17:3 ). with a stranger-- that is, for a friend (compare Pr 11:15 ; 17:18 ).
